title: Contributions of gluconeogenesis to glucose production in the fasted state
authors: Landau BR, Wahren J, Chandramouli V, Schumann WC, Ekberg K, Kalhan SC
population: Healthy adults, six women and two men aged 24 to 39 years, who ate at least 200 g of carbohydrate daily for 4 days and a meal of 12 to 14 kcal/kg at 5 p.m. before the fast
funder: This study was supported by National Institutes of Health grants DK-14507 and P50 HD-11089 and grant 89-0418 from the Bank of Sweden Tercentenary Foundation.
result: Deuterated water method, ratio of 2H enrichment at carbon 5 to carbon 2 of blood glucose. Gluconeogenesis contributed 47 ± 4% of glucose production after 14 h, 67 ± 4% after 22 h and 93 ± 2% after 42 h of fasting (mean ± SE, corrected for glycogen branch points; the PubMed abstract prints 47 +/- 49% and 67 +/- 41%). Plasma glucose was 5.2 ± 0.1 mmol/L at 14 h and 4.3 ± 0.1 mmol/L at 42 h; blood 3-hydroxybutyrate was 76 ± 25 µmol/L at 14 h and 1127 ± 153 µmol/L at 42 h.
